deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a typed page, numbered 90, from a French philosophical and psychological manuscript. Its language ('psyché', 'âme', 'inconscient profond / moyen-profond', 'peur primordiale', and mathematics as 'la belle dame') matches Grothendieck's reflective writings of the mid-to-late 1980s, the circle of La Clef des Songes and its Notes. It appears to have been filed (or its other side reused) among the stacks notes of cote 105. The exact source text is not certain.

The argument runs as follows:
- Sex is everywhere in the psyche. Conversely, the psyche and soul are everywhere in reality, at least in reality as perceived, since the image of reality is as much a creation of the soul as a reflection of an objective reality, whose existence is not denied.
- So fear of oneself and flight from oneself extend to fear and flight before all reality. Reality acts as a mirror in which the psyche sees itself, mostly unconsciously.
- The reaction is stronger the 'closer' the reality is: oneself, a parent, a spouse, a child. Above all, it depends on the intensity of the investment.
- Lofty philosophical speculation about God and the soul returns only a pale image. Even mathematics, if one's relation to 'la belle dame' is ardent, becomes neuralgic and returns a vivid self-image that provokes visceral fear.

The mathematics lives on the neighbouring pages. They treat a Mayer–Vietoris situation for an open cover U ∪ U' = X: a map to the three-point poset Ψ = Δ¹×Δ¹ minus (1,1), the associated split cofibred category over Ψ, properness of the projection to Ψ, and computing the pushforward fibrewise as H_D(U∩U'), H_D(U), H_D(U'). That material is in the context of basic localizers W and W_D (Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs territory), but it is not on this page.
errors: No mathematical content. Small grammatical slips in the typescript: 'des spéculations philosophique' should be 'philosophiques'; 'questions ... que l'esprit humain se soit jamais posé' should be 'posées'.

ideas.what: Psychological reflection: reality as a mirror of the psyche; fear and flight from self extend to all reality; mathematics ('la belle dame') can become a neuralgic mirror when the investment is intense.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's own meditative writings (themes close to Récoltes et Semailles and La Clef des Songes)
ideas.where_published: Thematically close to La Clef des Songes / Notes pour la Clef des Songes (circulated, not formally published); exact passage unidentified

transcription_corrections: Handwritten correction on line 'à un parent, au conjoint, à notre enfant': 'au' and 'notre' are manuscript corrections over the typescript.
'haut vol, aurant beau' is most likely corrected by hand to 'haut vol, auront beau' (a comma inserted after 'vol', a letter overwritten in 'aurant').
'niveau' is corrected by hand from a typo ('nivau').
'de cette réalité': 'cette' is a handwritten overstrike correction.
The '43' at the bottom left is the archival page number, not part of the text; '90' at the top is the typescript's own pagination.
